observation.def: One row of a data table: one person, market or image. ISLP counts them with \(i=1,\dots,n\).

variable-feature.def: One column of a data table. ISLP counts input variables with \(j=1,\dots,p\).

function.def: A rule that turns each input into exactly one output, written \(f(x)\) (ISLP) or \(\mathrm{f}[x]\) (Prince).

parameter.def: A number inside a model that training tunes and then fixes, such as a slope. Usually a Greek letter: \(\beta\), \(\phi\).

argmin.def: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x f(x)\) is the input \(x\) at which \(f\) is smallest (the min is the smallest value itself).

sigma-notation.def: \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i=a_1+a_2+\dots+a_n\): add the term for every value of the index.

transpose.def: \(\mathbf{A}^{\mathsf{T}}\): rows become columns. An \(m\times n\) matrix becomes \(n\times m\).

natural-log.def: \(\log y\) in both books: the power you raise \(e\approx2.718\) to in order to get \(y\). \(\log(ab)=\log a+\log b\).
